articles.title: France Says Europe Set to Release 42MM Barrels of Oil
articles.description: Europe will release 42 million barrels of oil reserves into the market over the next three months as part of its commitment to ease prices, France's economy minister Roland Lescure said.

articles.description: TotalEnergies reported $9.1 billion or $4.03 per diluted share in net profit adjusted for nonrecurring items for Q3, and expressed confidence high LNG prices and refining margins would continue to underpin results through the year.

articles.title: OEUK Says Budget 'Missed Bigger Opportunities'
articles.description: The 2026 UK Budget delivered by UK Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey on Wednesday 'missed bigger opportunities', industry body Offshore Energies UK said.

articles.title: TotalEnergies acquires 25% interest in 26 US offshore leases
articles.description: TotalEnergies has acquired a 25% working interest in 26 offshore exploration leases operated by Chevron in the US.

articles.title: UK National Grid to Extend France Power Link Operation to 2050
articles.description: UK’s National Grid plans to invest up to $532 million (£400 million) in extending the operation of the UK-France power interconnector until at least 2050 to preserve a vital electricity flexibility link. National Grid said on Thursday that after 40 years of operation to date, the Interconnexion France-Angleterre (IFA), the cross-border electricity link jointly owned by National Grid and French grid operator RTE, will see its life extended at least until 2050. articles.title: US approves $8.2bn ST LNG deepwater port off Texas coast
articles.description: The US Department of Transportation has approved a licence application for the construction and operation of an $8.2bn deepwater liquefied natural gas (LNG) port by ST LNG, to be built around 10.4 miles offshore Matagorda, Texas.

articles.title: Shell Approves $5B Buyback as Refining Boosts Profit
articles.description: Shell announced one of its highest-ever share buybacks as the Iran war and the Russia-Ukraine conflict lead to record margins for its oil-refining business and surging profits.

articles.title: Fragile Ukraine Truce Faces Critical Test Amid Fears of Forced Deportations
articles.description: A fragile cease-fire around Russian-occupied Oleshky entered its third day on October 29, offering hope to thousands of civilians facing severe shortages and perilous escape routes, amid fears that Russia could use the pause to forcibly transfer residents to Russia or occupied Crimea. The localized truce, brokered with the involvement of US First Lady Melania Trump, took effect on October 27 and is scheduled to last until November 1. articles.title: Iran War Hikes EU’s Oil Import Bill By $11 Billion Per Month
articles.description: The European Union has been paying $11 billion more to import oil since the Middle East crisis choked crude oil supplies and triggered a global fuel crisis, an analysis by Euronews Business showed on Thursday. The value of the EU’s petroleum imports jumped by 55.8% in the second quarter of 2026, despite the relatively stable volume of imports, according to Eurostat data. articles.title: Shell Profits Nearly Double to $10.8 Billion as Refining Margins Hit Record
articles.description: Record refining margins and higher LNG and gas prices boosted Shell’s third-quarter earnings to over $10.8 billion, nearly double compared to the same period last year, as the Middle East crisis squeezed fuel supplies and hiked oil and gas prices. Shell on Thursday reported adjusted earnings of $10.814 billion for the third quarter, the highest since 2022, almost double the $5.432 billion earnings a year ago. articles.title: Equinor swings to $2.5bn net income in Q3 2026
articles.description: Equinor has reported net income of $2.54bn for the third quarter of 2026 (Q3 2026), compared to a net loss of $204m in the same period last year.

articles.title: TotalEnergies Profit Doubles as War Boosts Refining and Trading
articles.description: TotalEnergies booked $9.1 billion in third-quarter adjusted net income, doubling earnings from a year earlier amid historically high refining margins, higher oil and gas prices, and strong oil and LNG trading. The French supermajor on Thursday reported an adjusted net income of $9.1 billion, up by 51% from the $6 billion profit for the second quarter, and 127% higher than the $4 billion booked for the third quarter of 2025. articles.title: Equinor Doubles Estimate for Major North Sea Gas Discovery
articles.description: The Afrodite gas discovery in the Norwegian North Sea may contain twice the volumes initially thought, operator Equinor said on Thursday after drilling a new appraisal well. Afrodite, discovered in 2008, is near the Kvitebjørn gas and condensate field and also close to the Gullfaks field in the North Sea, which is 15 kilometers (9.3 miles) away from Kvitebjørn. articles.title: EU Rules Out New Climate Finance Pledges at COP31
articles.description: The European Union will not be making new climate finance commitments at the upcoming COP31 conference, climate commissioner Wopke Hoekstra said, as quoted by Bloomberg today, describing the possibility of further financial commitments for emission reduction as “dead in the water”. The European Union has been the most generous climate finance provider globally for several years, but money has been tight lately, with other developments stealing the spotlight from emissions of carbon dioxide. articles.title: EU Scrambles to Contain Energy Price Crisis Ahead of Winter
articles.description: The energy ministers of EU member states are meeting today to discuss how to tackle a worsening energy price crisis as winter approaches, and with it, peak heating demand season. The meeting follows reports from Wednesday citing Energy Commissioner Dan Jorgensen as saying a series of refinery closures in EU member states over the past 20 years was a mistake as the diesel squeeze pushes prices to all-time highs. articles.description: Crude oil prices gave up some of the gains they made earlier this week, after U.S. Vice President JD Vance contacted the secretary of the Iranian Supreme National Security Council in a bid to restart peace talks. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $114.14 per barrel, and West Texas Intermediate was trading at $101.45 per barrel, both down from Wednesday but still significantly higher than they were at the start of October. articles.description: Oil rose as traders weighed whether the U.S. and Israel would resume military strikes on Iran.

articles.description: 'Short-term pain, right, for long-term gain. You're going to see very soon', Trump said at a rally in Corpus Christi.

articles.title: Oil Refineries Become Prime Targets as Global Fuel Shortage Worsens
articles.description: Ten years ago, European countries were closing refineries while Gulf oil states were building new ones. Now, many of these refineries have been damaged in the war between the U.S. and Israel, and Iran. Fuel output from one of the biggest refining regions is not going to be coming back soon. Neither is full refining capacity from one of the world’s top fuel exporters, Russia. articles.description: The tanker billed as the first to carry Russian diesel to the United States under Donald Trump’s deal with Vladimir Putin has dropped New York as its destination. articles.title: U.S. Natural Gas Production Hits New Records as Demand Surges
articles.description: U.S. natural gas production is on track to close a second consecutive year with record-high natural gas output as producers respond to demand signs both at home and overseas. Soaring demand for powering data centers in the United States and rising liquefied natural gas exports amid expanding liquefaction capacity, as well as surging global demand for spot LNG cargoes in the absence of Qatar’s gas due to the Iran war, are pushing American natural gas production higher this year. articles.title: Solar Has Overtaken Nuclear in the Global Power Mix
articles.description: Last year, solar power quietly overtook nuclear power in the global energy mix. This is a stunning feat when you consider that just a decade ago, in 2015, global solar generation amounted to just 256 terawatt-hours (TWh) in 2015, while global nuclear power generated ten-fold that amount at 2,576 TWh. And solar didn’t just overtake nuclear power in 2025; it surpassed it by a wide margin, producing 13 percent more energy worldwide.
